problem.description: Monotone stochastic variational inequality over a nonempty closed convex set.

variable_space.math: \text{Let }\mathbb{R}^n\text{ denote a finite dimensional vector space with inner product }\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle\text{ and norm }\|\cdot\|\text{ (not necessarily induced by }\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle\text{), and }Z\text{ be a nonempty closed convex set in }\mathbb{R}^n.

assumptions.name: J_subgradient_convex_simple
assumptions.math: J'(u)\in\partial J(u)\text{ is a subgradient of a relatively simple and convex function }J\text{ (see (4.5.9) below)}

assumptions.name: SFO_variance_bound
assumptions.math: \text{At the }i\text{-th call of SFOG and SFOH with input }z\in Z,\text{ the oracles SFOG and SFOH output stochastic information }G(z;\xi_i)\text{ and }H(z;\zeta_i)\text{ respectively, such that }\mathbb{E}\|G(u;\xi_i)-\nabla G(u)\|_*^2\le\sigma_G^2\ \text{and}\ \mathbb{E}\|H(u;\zeta_i)-H(u)\|_*^2\le\sigma_H^2,\text{ for some }\sigma_G,\sigma_H\ge0,\text{ where }\xi_i\text{ and }\zeta_i\text{ are independently distributed random samples.}

assumptions.name: Oracle_independence
assumptions.math: \xi_i\text{ and }\zeta_i\text{ are independently distributed random samples.}

assumptions.name: omega_distance_generating_function_on_Z
assumptions.math: V(\cdot,\cdot)\text{ is the prox-function associated with a distance generating function }\omega:Z\to\mathbb{R}\text{ given by }V(z,u):=\omega(u)-\omega(z)-\langle\nabla\omega(z),u-z\rangle,\ \forall u,z\in Z.

assumptions.name: Distance_generating_function_modulus_one_normalization
assumptions.math: \text{Without loss of generality, we assume that the strong convexity modulus }\sigma_\nu\text{ of }\nu\text{ is given by }1.

assumptions.name: Q_definition
assumptions.math: \text{For all }\tilde u,u\in Z,\text{ we define }Q(\tilde u,u):=G(\tilde u)-G(u)+\langle H(u),\tilde u-u\rangle+J(\tilde u)-J(u).

assumptions.name: Light_tail_oracle_noise
assumptions.math: \text{For any }i\text{-th call on oracles }SFOH\text{ and }SFOH\text{ with any input }u\in Z,\ \mathbb{E}[\exp\{\|\nabla G(u)-G(u;\xi_i)\|_*^2/\sigma_G^2\}]\le\exp\{1\},\ \text{and}\ \mathbb{E}[\exp\{\|H(u)-H(u;\zeta_i)\|_*^2/\sigma_H^2\}]\le\exp\{1\}.

main_theorem.statement_math: \text{Suppose that }\sup_{z_1,z_2\in Z}V(z_1,z_2)\le D_Z^2.\ \text{Also assume that the parameters }\{\alpha_t\}\text{ and }\{\gamma_t\}\text{ in Algorithm 4.4 satisfy }\alpha_1=1,\ q-L\alpha_t\gamma_t-3M^2\gamma_t^2\ge0\text{ for some }q\in(0,1),\text{ and }\frac{\alpha_t}{\Gamma_t\gamma_t}\le\frac{\alpha_{t+1}}{\Gamma_{t+1}\gamma_{t+1}},\ \forall t\ge1,\text{ where }\Gamma_t\text{ is defined in (4.5.17). Then, (a) Under Assumption 10, for all }t\ge1,\ \mathbb{E}[g(\bar w_{t+1})]\le Q_0(t):=\frac{2\alpha_t}{\gamma_t}D_Z^2+\left(4\sigma_H^2+\left(1+\frac{1}{2(1-q)}\right)\sigma_G^2\right)\Gamma_t\sum_{i=1}^t\frac{\alpha_i\gamma_i}{\Gamma_i}.\ \text{(b) Under Assumption 11, for all }\lambda>0\text{ and }t\ge1,\ \operatorname{Prob}\{g(\bar w_{t+1})>Q_0(t)+\lambda Q_1(t)\}\le2\exp\{-\lambda^2/3\}+3\exp\{-\lambda\},\text{ where }Q_1(t):=\Gamma_t(\sigma_G+\sigma_H)D_Z\sqrt{2\sum_{i=1}^t(\alpha_i/\Gamma_i)^2}+\left(4\sigma_H^2+\left(1+\frac{1}{2(1-q)}\right)\sigma_G^2\right)\Gamma_t\sum_{i=1}^t\frac{\alpha_i\gamma_i}{\Gamma_i}.
main_theorem.rate: With beta = O(sigma/D_Z), the number of iterations to find an epsilon-solution \bar w of (4.5.1) satisfying E[g(\bar w)] <= epsilon is O(L/epsilon + M/epsilon + sigma^2/epsilon^2), as stated in (4.5.56).
main_theorem.measure: Expected and high-probability bounds on the SVI gap function g(\bar w_{t+1}).
